title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIV: Garissoles 3 / Placeus — Calvin quia intra nos; before duplex question
pass_a_gloss: GAR. 3. When it is said that the corruption of our first parent is imputed to us his posterity, not insofar as it stuck in Adam himself, but insofar as it passed into us: what then is that reason of this matter which is at once brought forward; namely that our hereditary corruption is of the same species with the corruption which was in Adam? Does therefore that specific identity of the two corruptions effect this, that the prior is imputed to us? Which if it is so, nothing of a cause can be said why the corruption of all our ancestors should not be said to be imputed to us &c. PLAC. Here also he fashions for himself a monster which he may conquer. For that reason of mine he both truncates and wrongly interprets. He truncates: for he omits both the words immediately preceding, and that I may use Calvin's words, because it is within us, and the following, and that Adam communicated with us as his nature, so his moral corruption. He interprets badly: For I did not wish by those words, For our hereditary corruption is the same in species with that which once was in Adam, to give a reason why Adam's sin accepted in the third mode is imputed to us; but why it is said to be within us. Why it is imputed I showed when I said, and that I may use Calvin's words, because it is within us: which causal because could have warned him, if he had been willing to attend. I said therefore with Calvin on Rom. 5:17 that it is therefore imputed, because it is within us: But that it can be said to be within us, because our hereditary corruption is the same in species with that which was in Adam. And that I illustrated by a likeness drawn from our nature itself, which, because it is the same in species with Adam's nature, and propagated from it, thence it comes about that Adam can be said to have communicated his nature with us: but no less did he communicate with us his corruption, or sin. Therefore Adam's sin can be said to have been propagated into us, to have entered into us, to be within us. This is the force of my reasoning; from which you see, Reader, how far D. Garissoles wanders.
pass_b_english: Garissoles: (3) When our first parent's corruption is said to be imputed to us his posterity not as it stuck in Adam himself but as it passed into us, what is that reason instantly offered—namely that our hereditary corruption is of the same species as the corruption that was in Adam? Does that specific identity of the two corruptions make the former imputed to us? If so, nothing can explain why the corruption of all our ancestors should not likewise be said to be imputed to us, and so on. Placeus: Here too he invents a monster to slay. He both truncates my reason and misreads it. He truncates: he omits the words immediately before—and, to use Calvin's phrasing, "because it is within us"—and what follows: that Adam shared with us both his nature and his moral corruption. He misreads: by those words "For our hereditary corruption is the same in species as that which once was in Adam" I did not mean to explain why Adam's sin in the third sense is imputed to us, but why it is said to be within us. Why it is imputed I showed when I said, again with Calvin, "because it is within us"—a causal "because" that could have warned him had he cared to listen. So with Calvin on Romans 5:17 I said it is imputed because it is within us; and that it can be called within us because our hereditary corruption is the same in species as that which was in Adam. I illustrated that by a likeness from our very nature: since it is the same in species as Adam's and propagated from him, Adam can be said to have shared his nature with us—and no less his corruption, or sin. So Adam's sin can be said to have been propagated into us, to have entered us, to be within us. That is the force of my reasoning; from it, reader, you see how far Dr. Garissoles strays.
source_text:
GAR. 3. Quando dicitur primi nostri parentis corruptio nobis posteris illius imputari, non quatenus haesit in ipso Adamo, sed quatenus transiit in nos: quanam est illa, quae statim profertur, hujus rei ratio; quod scilicet corruptio nostra haereditaria, sit ejusdem speciei cum corruptione, quae fuit in Adamo? An igitur specifica illa duarum corruptionum identitas id efficit, ut prior nobis imputetur? Quod si est, nihil causae dici potest, cur non omnium nostrorum majorum corruptio nobis imputari dicenda sit &c.

PLAC. Hic quoque monstrum sibi fingit, quod debellet. Meam enim istam rationem & truncat, & perperam interpretatur. Truncat: omittit enim & verba immediate praecedentia, ac ut verbis utar Calvini, quia intra nos est, & sequentia, ac quam suam naturam, tam suam corruptionem moralem nobiscum Adamus communicavit. Male interpretatur: Non enim verbis illis, Est enim corruptio nostra haereditaria eadem specie cum illa quae olim fuit in Adamo, rationem reddere volui, cur peccatum Adami tertio modo acceptum nobis imputetur; sed cur dicatur intra nos esse. Quare imputetur ostendi, cum dixi, ac ut verbis utar Calvini, quia intra nos est: id quod causalis quia monere eum potuisset, si voluisset attendere. Dixi ergo cum Calvino ad Rom. 5. 17. ideo imputari, quia intra nos est: Posse autem intra nos dici, quia corruptio nostra haereditaria est eadem specie cum illa quae fuit in Adamo. Idque illustravi similitudine ducta ab ipsa natura nostra, quae, quia specie eadem est cum natura Adami, & ab ea propagata, inde fit ut dici possit Adamus naturam suam nobiscum communicasse: non minus autem nobiscum communicavit corruptionem suam, seu peccatum. Potest igitur dici peccatum Adami in nos propagatum, in nos introiisse, intra nos esse. Haec est ratiocinii mei vis; a qua vides, Lector, quam aberret D. Garissolius.
